pr_title: test(e2e::storage): avoid deleting primary and driver namespace twice
pr_body:
Signed-off-by: knight42 <anonymousknight96@gmail.com>

**What type of PR is this?**

/kind flake

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

As described in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/94221#issuecomment-680147677, the root cause is the namespace would be deleted twice in the test, it is more obvious if we take a closer look at the access log of apiserver:
```
# created namespace "provisioning-9612" in test "subPath should support existing single file"
45875:I0824 21:48:27.739634       9 httplog.go:89] "HTTP" verb="POST" URI="/api/v1/namespaces" latency="10.521185ms" userAgent="e2e.test/v1.20.0 (linux/amd64) kubernetes/3229073 -- [sig-storage] In-tree Volumes [Driver: local][LocalVolumeType: dir] [Testpattern: Pre-provisioned PV (default fs)] subPath should support existing single file [LinuxOnly]" srcIP="34.121.82.231:58558" resp=201

# deleted namespace "provisioning-9612" in test "subPath should support existing single file"
122918:I0824 21:52:03.923611       9 httplog.go:89] "HTTP" verb="DELETE" URI="/api/v1/namespaces/provisioning-9612" latency="5.37683ms" userAgent="e2e.test/v1.20.0 (linux/amd64) kubernetes/3229073 -- [sig-storage] CSI Volumes [Driver: csi-hostpath] [Testpattern: Dynamic PV (default fs)] subPath should support existing single file [LinuxOnly]" srcIP="34.121.82.231:58578" resp=200

# created namespace "provisioning-9612" in test "subPath should support file as subpath"
127903:I0824 21:52:18.766531       9 httplog.go:89] "HTTP" verb="POST" URI="/api/v1/namespaces" latency="3.974101ms" userAgent="e2e.test/v1.20.0 (linux/amd64) kubernetes/3229073 -- [sig-storage] In-tree Volumes [Driver: gluster] [Testpattern: Pre-provisioned PV (default fs)] subPath should support file as subpath [LinuxOnly]" srcIP="34.121.82.231:33176" resp=201

# deleted namespace "provisioning-9612" in test "subPath should support existing single file"
130263:I0824 21:52:28.584696       9 httplog.go:89] "HTTP" verb="DELETE" URI="/api/v1/namespaces/provisioning-9612" latency="13.93603ms" userAgent="e2e.test/v1.20.0 (linux/amd64) kubernetes/3229073 -- [sig-storage] CSI Volumes [Driver: csi-hostpath] [Testpattern: Dynamic PV (default fs)] subPath should support existing single file [LinuxOnly]" srcIP="34.121.82.231:58578" resp=200

# deleted namespace "provisioning-9612" in test "subPath should support file as subpath"
132603:I0824 21:52:37.288535       9 httplog.go:89] "HTTP" verb="DELETE" URI="/api/v1/namespaces/provisioning-9612" latency="2.292099ms" userAgent="e2e.test/v1.20.0 (linux/amd64) kubernetes/3229073 -- [sig-storage] In-tree Volumes [Driver: gluster] [Testpattern: Pre-provisioned PV (default fs)] subPath should support file as subpath [LinuxOnly]" srcIP="34.121.82.231:33176" resp=200
```

Perhaps I am missing something, but I think we don't need to delete the namespace during the test, as the namespace would be deleted after the test: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/4db3a096ce8ac730b2280494422e1c4cf5fe875e/test/e2e/framework/framework.go#L375-L395

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

Fixes #94221

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:

```release-note
NONE
```

@Jiawei0227 It looks like we don't need to delete the driver namespace during testing as well, because the driver namespace is created by `Framework.CreateNamespace()`, so the namespace would be deleted after test: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/4db3a096ce8ac730b2280494422e1c4cf5fe875e/test/e2e/framework/framework.go#L482-L485

> @gnufied If driver namespace is deleted before deleting the test namespace then pods in test namespace will be stuck in "terminating" state because CSI driver that is responsible for unmounting volumes will not be available.

then I think we are good, as we create the primary namespace first then the driver namespace, they would be deleted in the same order: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/4db3a096ce8ac730b2280494422e1c4cf5fe875e/test/e2e/framework/framework.go#L383-L386

> then I think we are good, as we create the primary namespace first then the driver namespace, they would be deleted in the same order: 

No the code you linked deletes the namespaces without waiting for them, so it is as good as deleting the driver namespace and test namespace almost together.

> No the code you linked deletes the namespaces without waiting for them, so it is as good as deleting the driver namespace and test namespace almost together.

yeah but I think we could wait for the deletion and still avoid deleting the namespace twice.

I am putting this on hold so as concerns about csi driver cleanup are addressed properly. 

/hold

Another point is - there are other tests that delete the namespace in their own test suite. I think it is not realistic that nobody other than framework.AfterEach should delete the nameapce.  If we had namespace collision bug then, we should address that directly rather than doing what this PR proposes.

> If we had namespace collision bug then, we should address that directly rather than doing what this PR proposes.

IMHO this is not a namespace collision bug, from the access log of apiserver I gave above:
```
# created namespace "provisioning-9612" in test "subPath should support existing single file"
45875:I0824 21:48:27.739634       9 httplog.go:89] "HTTP" verb="POST" URI="/api/v1/namespaces" latency="10.521185ms" userAgent="e2e.test/v1.20.0 (linux/amd64) kubernetes/3229073 -- [sig-storage] In-tree Volumes [Driver: local][LocalVolumeType: dir] [Testpattern: Pre-provisioned PV (default fs)] subPath should support existing single file [LinuxOnly]" srcIP="34.121.82.231:58558" resp=201

# deleted namespace "provisioning-9612" in test "subPath should support existing single file"
122918:I0824 21:52:03.923611       9 httplog.go:89] "HTTP" verb="DELETE" URI="/api/v1/namespaces/provisioning-9612" latency="5.37683ms" userAgent="e2e.test/v1.20.0 (linux/amd64) kubernetes/3229073 -- [sig-storage] CSI Volumes [Driver: csi-hostpath] [Testpattern: Dynamic PV (default fs)] subPath should support existing single file [LinuxOnly]" srcIP="34.121.82.231:58578" resp=200

# created namespace "provisioning-9612" in test "subPath should support file as subpath"
127903:I0824 21:52:18.766531       9 httplog.go:89] "HTTP" verb="POST" URI="/api/v1/namespaces" latency="3.974101ms" userAgent="e2e.test/v1.20.0 (linux/amd64) kubernetes/3229073 -- [sig-storage] In-tree Volumes [Driver: gluster] [Testpattern: Pre-provisioned PV (default fs)] subPath should support file as subpath [LinuxOnly]" srcIP="34.121.82.231:33176" resp=201

# deleted namespace "provisioning-9612" in test "subPath should support existing single file"
130263:I0824 21:52:28.584696       9 httplog.go:89] "HTTP" verb="DELETE" URI="/api/v1/namespaces/provisioning-9612" latency="13.93603ms" userAgent="e2e.test/v1.20.0 (linux/amd64) kubernetes/3229073 -- [sig-storage] CSI Volumes [Driver: csi-hostpath] [Testpattern: Dynamic PV (default fs)] subPath should support existing single file [LinuxOnly]" srcIP="34.121.82.231:58578" resp=200
```
It is literally valid for another test to use namespace `provisioning-9612` as this namespace does not exist before from its point of view, it is the second deletion that cause another test to fail.

> I think it is not realistic that nobody other than framework.AfterEach should delete the nameapce

I generally agree this point, but now that we create the namespace by calling `Framework.CreateNamespace()`, and `Framework.CreateNamespace()` would make this namespace to be deleted after the test, I think we don't need to bother deleting it manually.

I kind of agree with @knight42 idea of only deleting the namespace by `framework.AfterEach`. In my opinion, whoever creates the namespace should be responsible for cleanup the resources. So since framework added the namespace, we should let the framework do its work.  

My question for @gnufied is that is there any special reason we have to delete it twice? Because the root cause for this issue is the twice deletion of the namespace. Unless there is concern about the resource not getting cleanup correctly, I think it is reasonable to handle the namespace deletion to the framework.

/test pull-kubernetes-conformance-kind-ipv6-parallel

@gnufied Are you satisfied with this change https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/94247/commits/8779bd00bcc40d0be905402f28cd371fb742cb92?

@knight42 No it does not fixes that. The interaction we are trying to fix is kind of subtle. framework's AfterEach and AfterSuite can race with each other in certain cases(when interrupted for example) and in that case the defer/AfterEach within the test will start executing first and will remove the driver without waiting for the test pods to be deleted and that in turn would prevent deletion of test pods and hence causes resource leakage in case e2e timesout. 

@Jiawei0227 I have tried fixing the namespace being deleted twice bug with https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/94318 . The main issue to consider is how AfterEach and AfterSuite can race with each other. I have tried to document this https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/91689#issue-426705225 and in inline comments.

feels like a test only problem like @liggitt said. We don't even have gluster in our CI/prow to test against...

cc @msau42 @xing-yang 

Michelle, Xing, Can you please confirm that this is not a blocker for 1.19.0?

Knowing the timeframe for when the test started and when that delete happened would be interesting to know. Possibilities I can see:
* something in the test timed out, and the cleanup happened in parallel with something in the test attempting to run
* multiple tests are reusing the same test context and namespace name at the same time (I can never keep straight how ginkgo parallel tests work)
@dims This does not look like a blocker for 1.19.0.

Thanks @xing-yang!

/milestone v1.20
@liggitt looking at the logs it seems to be the latter "same test context and namespace name at the same time", but we can deal with this for 1.19.1

cc @gnufied @Jiawei0227 
This looks like another instance of "the same test namespace is being reused". I believe @Jiawei0227 had a mitigation for that to try to make the namespaces more unique.
(btw, the test brings up a containerized gluster server so we are exercising gluster functionality)

Yeah, looking at the build log found that it is the same issue as #93749 
The issue is still around the double deletion of namespace, i.e. we delete the test namespace during the test execution, but later on the `AfterEach` call we delete the namespace again to ensure it truly get cleaned up. But unfortunately, this namespace has been reused by another test case between this gap.

Some potential fix I can think of:
1. Since deletion of the primary namespace twice is inevitable, maybe we should consider generate primary namespace based on a hashing of the test cases name?
2. Extends the 4 digits random namespace to 6, this should not solve the problem in nature but it will extremely decrease the chance it happens.
3. Consider using an in-memory namespace map to keep record of already generated namespaces for the whole test run and refuse to generate the same namespace again in the whole lifecycle of a prow job.
@Jiawei0227 do you know if this gluster test is using your mitigation in #93869?

1. A hash of the testcase name + random suffix (because tests can be run multiple times) seems like a good way to mitigate the chances of tests reusing the same namespace. I'm unsure if we know the test case name at the time of test namespace creation though.

2. Otherwise I think increasing the length of the random suffix is a quick and easy mitigation

3. I believe ginkgo [spawns multiple processes](https://onsi.github.io/ginkgo/#parallel-specs) to run in parallel, so this may not work
Yes it is. But my fix in #93869 can only reduce the chance of collision and probably improve readability of logs. But not to eliminate this issue in nature.

AFAICT https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/93869 does not affect intree code at all, because it only fixes namespace of driver.  If we are seeing collision of primary namespace for intree code then it is a different problem.

1. Fix on #93869 only deals with the collision between test namespace and driver namespace. And that fix is taking affect.
2. This failure is because a test namespace collides with another test namespace. And this is not related to in-tree code at all. Any test could potentially become flaky because their namespace can be deleted during test execution. It's just happens to be this intree test this time. The root cause for this problem is: 

We cleaned up the test namespace twice which gives it a small gap that another testcase can generate the same namespace and be affected by the second namespace deletion from the original testcase.

/assign 

I would like to give it a shot.
I've opened #94247 to address this issue.

/unassign

/assign @gnufied

review_comments: We have to delete the namespace here as per comments from @gnufied in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/93749#issuecomment-670653716

> We have to delete the first namespace (which includes test pods), otherwise if you delete them after deleting the driver pods - we will have pods stuck forever in terminating state.

I am a bit curious why the pods would stuck forever?
Alternaltively could we cleanup the pods in the namespace rather than deleting the namespace?

Looks like the job `pull-kubernetes-e2e-gce-ubuntu-containerd` passed even if we do not delete the namespace twice: https://prow.k8s.io/view/gcs/kubernetes-jenkins/pr-logs/pull/94247/pull-kubernetes-e2e-gce-ubuntu-containerd/1298528224002707456/

I added https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/94247#issuecomment-680847436 why we can't skip deleting the namespace.

Another way of fixing this is to ensure that if primary namespace is deleted elsewhere then it is removed from `namespacesToDelete` array. But if we do that, one thing to keep in mind is - in case of failure etc, namespace information must still be dumped.
